observation.visible_scene: Outdoor setting against a white brick wall with green grass. A pale wooden plank rests horizontally on top of a tree stump. A DAB-brand beer can stands upright near the center of the plank. A person (blue jeans, orange work glove) on the left holds an orange multi-pronged claw/fork-like tool. A stream of white foamy liquid is already spurting from a hole on the left side of the can at the first frame, running down onto the plank and dripping off its left edge onto the stump.
visible_changes: The gloved hand repeatedly drives the orange tool toward the can's left side, makes brief contact (poking/stabbing), then pulls it back to the left; this advance-and-retreat cycle occurs several times across the excerpt.

At each contact moment the white liquid splashes outward more violently from the hole, while between contacts the liquid continues as a steady arcing stream that flows down the plank edge and off onto the stump.
The can stays upright on the plank throughout; only minor shifts in tilt are visible, and the plank remains level on the stump.
The background (brick wall, vertical posts, grass) holds a constant position across frames, indicating the camera is essentially static rather than panning.
Droplets of white liquid scatter into the air near the can during strikes and fall toward the grass on the left.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the hole in the can and the origin of the already-flowing stream (the spurt is ongoing at frame 1, before any visible tool contact in this segment).
The exact identity of the orange tool and of the white liquid (beer/foam vs. another fluid).
What happens after the last frame (whether the can eventually tips, empties, or the action stops).
uncertain_details: Whether each tool strike enlarges the hole or merely agitates the existing flow cannot be confirmed from the frames.
The tool's prongs appear bent/flexible in some frames; this may be deformation or motion blur.
Small differences in can orientation between frames could be slight real tilt or perspective from the tool's contact, not a full topple.
